items.stem: Which best distinguishes threat intelligence from raw threat data?

options.text: Intelligence is analysed and contextualised to support a decision
options.rationale: Correct: analysis and context turn data into intelligence.

options.text: Intelligence is simply a larger list of indicators
options.rationale: Volume alone does not make data into intelligence.
Intelligence commonly draws on many sources.
Automation aids but does not define intelligence.

items.explanation: Correct: analysis and context for a decision distinguish intelligence from data.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO are higher-value than a single IP address when tracking an adversary? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: behaviours are harder for an adversary to change than an IP.

options.text: A documented attack pattern mapped to a framework
options.rationale: Correct: mapped patterns persist across infrastructure changes.

options.text: A one-off IP that may rotate hourly
options.rationale: Single IPs are easily changed and low-value alone.

options.text: The colour of the attacker's website
options.rationale: Cosmetic details carry no defensive value.

items.explanation: Correct: TTPs and mapped attack patterns outlast easily changed indicators.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: A single vendor blog claims a new campaign but no other source corroborates it. How should it be treated?

options.text: As an uncorroborated lead with lower confidence pending verification
options.rationale: Correct: single-source, uncorroborated reporting warrants lower confidence.

options.text: As confirmed fact to act on immediately
options.rationale: A single uncorroborated source does not justify high confidence.
It is a lead worth verifying, not dismissing outright.

options.text: As more reliable than government reporting
options.rationale: Reliability depends on corroboration, not on being a blog.

items.explanation: Correct: uncorroborated single-source reporting should carry lower confidence.
